summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Hong Kong CIES / New CIES documents (ImmD annual-report chapters and appendices, ImmD CIES statistics pages and web pages, LegCo brief, FSTB press release). Most programme numbers were already in the dataset; this pass adds the CPA-report counts and shares (2009-2014), CIES visas for 2022-2023, the 2010 announcement's cumulative admissions and investment, New CIES enquiries, and net-asset and threshold rule rows.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.quote: demonstrating that he/she has net assets of not less than HK$30 million (or equivalent in foreign currencies) to which he/she is absolutely beneficially entitled throughout the two years preceding the application
program_terms.notes: Eligibility condition, not an investment. The brief gives no start date (it says the scheme is to open 'in mid-2024', para 26); valid_from follows the launch date in the dataset (1 Mar 2024, hkg-investhk-pr-new-cies-opens-2024) and valid_to the day before the six-month rule took effect (hkg-fstb-pr-new-cies-enhancements-2025). Same brief: non-residential real estate counts for at most HK$10 million (para 7(g)); certificates of deposit capped at 10% of the minimum investment threshold (para 7(c)).

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the six months before applying
program_terms.quote: net assets or net equity to which he/she is absolutely beneficially entitled with a market value of not less than HK$30 million net throughout six months (two years before the enhancement) preceding the application
program_terms.notes: Eligibility condition, not an investment. From 1 March 2025 jointly owned net assets count for the applicant's share (section 1(a)(ii)), and investments may be held through a family-owned investment holding vehicle (section 1(b)).

program_terms.quote: The threshold of investment (and Net assets/Net equity requirement) for admission to Hong Kong under the CIES is raised from HK$6.5 million to HK$10 million
program_terms.notes: Real estate suspended as a permissible asset class from the same date. Transitional rule: new applications with investment (including real estate) of at least HK$6.5 million made within the six months before 14 Oct 2010 were still eligible under the old rules. Same threshold applies to the net-asset requirement. The threshold was to be reviewed every three years. valid_to not given here (scheme suspended 15 Jan 2015, see hkg-immd-cies-page-2026).

program_terms.location: Before Applying, Eligibility Criteria and footnote *
program_terms.quote: not less than HK$10 million* in permissible investment asset classes
program_terms.notes: Investment within six months before applying or within six months after approval-in-principle (certificates of deposit only after). Footnote: 'The investment threshold (and Net assets or Net equity requirement) has been raised from HK$6.5 million to HK$10 million with effect from 14 October 2010.' valid_to: the page says the scheme 'has been suspended since 15 January 2015'.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.quote: have net assets of not less than HK$10 million* to which he is absolutely beneficially entitled throughout the two years preceding his application
program_terms.notes: Eligibility condition, not an investment. Raised from HK$6.5 million on 14 October 2010 (footnote). Applicants could optionally use a CPA (Practising) report to show it.

program_terms.applies_to: applicant's net assets, held throughout the two years before applying
program_terms.quote: The investment threshold (and Net assets or Net equity requirement) has been raised from HK$6.5 million to HK$10 million with effect from 14 October 2010.
program_terms.notes: Start date not given on this page (the scheme opened on 27 Oct 2003 per hkg-isd-pr-cies-launch-2003). The two-year holding period is stated for the current (HK$10m) rule only.

events.title: Accountant's report on net assets made optional
events.description: To shorten processing, CIES applicants may choose whether to hire a Certified Public Accountant (Practising) to prepare the financial report showing they meet the net-asset requirement.
events.location: Chapter text, section 'Capital Investment Entrant Scheme'
events.quote: To shorten the processing time of the applications under the Scheme, with effect from March 16, 2009, applicants may decide on their own whether or not to hire a Certified Public Accountant (Practising)

events.title: Insurers allowed as CIES financial intermediaries
events.description: Together with the HK$10 million threshold and the suspension of real estate, insurers authorised for Class C (linked long-term) business may act as the financial intermediary holding an entrant's designated investment account.
events.location: paragraph 'Furthermore, with effect from the commencement date ...'
events.quote: Furthermore, with effect from the commencement date, an insurer authorised to carry on Class C business as specified in Part 2 of the First Schedule to the Insurance Companies Ordinance is permitted to act as a financial intermediary for the purpose of the CIES.

new_indicators.name: Enquiries received by the programme
new_indicators.definition: Number of enquiries (phone, email, visits, as the source counts them) received by the programme authority from prospective applicants in a period. Not applications.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-hkg1 for the Hong Kong New CIES press release of 7 Jan 2025 ('Number of enquiries Nearly 7 000' in the first 10 months).

ledger.contains: Legislative Council Brief of 19 Dec 2023 on the New CIES: eligibility (age 18+, eligible nationalities, net assets of HK$30m for two years, no adverse record), minimum investment HK$30m (HK$27m permissible assets incl. non-residential real estate capped at HK$10m and certificates of deposit capped at 10%, plus HK$3m in the CIES Investment Portfolio), portfolio maintenance rules, procedure (InvestHK then ImmD; visitor entry up to 180 days to invest; 24-month then 3-year stays; permanent residence after 7 years), buyer's and new residential stamp duty suspension for applicants, implications, planned launch mid-2024. No application statistics. Investment thresholds, Exco approval and the Budget announcement were already recorded; this pass adds the net-asset requirement as a rule row (caps noted in it).

InvestHK/FSTB press release of 7 Jan 2025: New CIES enhancements effective 1 Mar 2025 (six-month net-asset test instead of two years, jointly owned assets, holding through a family-owned investment holding vehicle or special purpose entity) and key figures for the first 10 months (enquiries nearly 7,000; applications over 800; 733 passed the net-asset check; 240 passed the investment check; expected investment over HK$24 billion). Also a statement that applications in the first 10 months exceeded those in the same period of the original CIES (no number). The four application figures and the rule-change event were already recorded; this pass adds the enquiries figure (new indicator proposed) and the six-month net-asset rule row.

ImmD web announcement (archived Dec 2012) of the CIES rule amendments from 14 Oct 2010: threshold and net-asset requirement raised from HK$6.5m to HK$10m, real estate suspended, Class C insurers allowed as financial intermediaries, three-yearly review, transitional rule for investments made in the six months before; share of entrants who invested before applying (around 11%); cumulative admissions since 2003 (around 8,200 investors, 15,500 dependants, around $58bn); and the separate 6 Jul 2010 refinement admitting investment-linked assurance products (event already recorded). The 14 Oct 2010 threshold change is already an event from hkg-isd-pr-cies-amended-2010. This pass adds the four numbers, the HK$10m rule row and the intermediary event.

ImmD web page on the (suspended) CIES, revised 16 Apr 2026: suspended since 15 Jan 2015; New CIES launched 1 Mar 2024; eligible persons; eligibility (net assets and investment of HK$10m, raised from HK$6.5m on 14 Oct 2010); permissible asset classes; portfolio maintenance; conditions of stay (3+3 months as visitor, 2 years then 3-year extensions, right of abode after 7 years); extension-of-stay procedure; fees by reference to a fee table not included in the stored page. No statistics. The suspension and New CIES launch events are already recorded; this pass adds the HK$10m investment and net-asset rule rows and the earlier HK$6.5m net-asset row.
